hyperedges.label: RAG flow: browser upload -> chat proxy -> embedding-server chunking/embedding -> pgvector -> retrieval
MCP contract: chat client profile, mcp-server endpoint, and the docs:// resource protocol
Container-backed state: pinned compose project, named volumes, datasource, idempotent schema, tests opting out

nodes.label: Multi-module Maven project (Java 25, claude-parent)
nodes.rationale: Parent aggregator carries dependencyManagement only, with no inherited <dependencies>, so each module declares exactly the artifacts it uses without versions. Versions are pinned in the parent only for artifacts no BOM manages (anthropic-java-core, okhttp, okio, mcp-core).

nodes.label: chat module (Spring Boot app, port 8080)
nodes.rationale: Holds Claude chat, tools, file analysis, the web UI and the RAG *client* side only; it deliberately owns no embedding model and no vector store implementation.

nodes.label: embedding-server module (Spring Boot app, port 8081)
nodes.rationale: Owns the Ollama embedding model, the pgvector store, chunking/ingestion and compose.yaml, so the embedding stack lives in exactly one module.

nodes.label: mcp-server module (Spring Boot app, port 8082)
nodes.rationale: Only this module declares the MCP *server* starter, so only it serves /mcp and the other apps no longer need a spring.ai.mcp.server.enabled: false guard. It owns no model and no database.

nodes.label: RAG split (chat retrieves over HTTP, embedding-server embeds and stores)
nodes.rationale: Under the rag profile chat builds a read-only VectorStore whose similaritySearch POSTs to /api/embeddings/search, and QuestionAnswerAdvisor retrieves through it. Filters travel as Spring AI filter DSL text (printed, re-parsed server-side) so no serialized filter objects cross the wire. Writes through the client-side store throw UnsupportedOperationException by design; a controller proxies /api/ai/documents to /api/embeddings/documents so the browser stays single-origin.
nodes.norm_label: rag split (chat retrieves over http, embedding-server embeds and stores)

nodes.label: Keep unused autoconfiguration off the classpath, not excluded
nodes.rationale: A module declares only the starters it needs, so there is nothing to switch off — preferred over spring.ai.model.*: none guards or spring.autoconfigure.exclude. chat declares the vector-store SPI but no store implementation and no JDBC driver.
nodes.norm_label: keep unused autoconfiguration off the classpath, not excluded

nodes.label: Declare an artifact explicitly whenever its classes are imported
nodes.rationale: Transitive-only artifacts show as unresolved imports in IntelliJ and the transitive path can vanish on upgrade. Trimming can also silently drop autoconfiguration: chat needs an explicit spring-boot-restclient because spring-boot-starter-web does not provide RestClient.Builder. Verify a trim by starting each app — contextLoads does not cover the rag profile.
nodes.norm_label: declare an artifact explicitly whenever its classes are imported

nodes.label: Nearest-definition mediation downgrade hazard (victools pinned to 5.x)
nodes.rationale: Declaring an artifact directly moves its transitives one hop closer and can win Maven's nearest-definition mediation, downgrading a shared library. anthropic-java-core ships com.github.victools 4.38.0; once chat declared the SDK directly, tool calling died at runtime with NoClassDefFoundError JacksonSchemaModule while every test passed. Check dependency:tree -Dverbose for 'omitted for conflict' resolving to an older version.
nodes.norm_label: nearest-definition mediation downgrade hazard (victools pinned to 5.x)

nodes.label: Each app must run with its own module directory as working directory
nodes.rationale: spring-boot-docker-compose resolves compose.yaml against the process working directory, as does ./workspace (chat's text-editor base dir). mvnw -pl <module> spring-boot:run already defaults to ${project.basedir}; IntelliJ needs Working directory = $MODULE_WORKING_DIR$ or Boot fails with 'No Docker Compose file found in directory <repo root>'.
nodes.norm_label: each app must run with its own module directory as working directory

nodes.label: MCP client gated by the mcp profile (starter inert without it)
nodes.rationale: chat declares spring-ai-starter-mcp-client unconditionally but keeps connections in application-mcp.yaml, so chat never hard-depends on mcp-server being up. Remote ToolCallbacks are collected via ObjectProvider (empty when the profile is off) and attached per request with spec.toolCallbacks(...) alongside annotated tool beans via spec.tools(...). Local tool enable/disable switches do not cover MCP tools — those are all-or-nothing with the profile.
nodes.norm_label: mcp client gated by the mcp profile (starter inert without it)

nodes.label: @<uri> MCP resource reference resolution in chat input
nodes.rationale: MCP resources are client-driven so they need a path of their own: @docs://mcp-server/README.md references are read through McpSyncClient and prepended in a <referenced-resources> block. It hooks the single buildPromptSpec so blocking and streaming both get it, and unresolvable references become inline error entries rather than exceptions. resources/list returns fixed resources plus templates, so concrete document URIs come from reading the listing resource itself.
nodes.norm_label: @<uri> mcp resource reference resolution in chat input

nodes.label: Centralized Spring AI BOM version management
nodes.rationale: spring-ai-bom 2.0.0-RC2 imported in the parent dependencyManagement so modules add Spring AI starters without versions; spring-boot-maven-plugin is version-managed in pluginManagement and enabled (repackage) per application module.
nodes.norm_label: centralized spring ai bom version management

nodes.label: Maven wrapper build and run commands (reactor from repo root)
nodes.rationale: Use ./mvnw so no separately installed Maven is needed; a Java version mismatch is resolved with the java-switch skill via SDKMAN rather than by lowering the project's Java 25 requirement.
nodes.norm_label: maven wrapper build and run commands (reactor from repo root)

nodes.label: Maven parent overrides (empty license/developers elements)
nodes.rationale: Maven inherits unwanted elements like <license> and <developers> from the parent POM, so the project POM carries empty overrides; the overrides must be removed if the parent is switched and inheritance is actually wanted.

nodes.label: Spring AI Anthropic Claude reference documentation (cited)
nodes.norm_label: spring ai anthropic claude reference documentation (cited)

nodes.label: chat MCP client config (SYNC, 30s timeout, toolcallback enabled)
nodes.rationale: type: SYNC matches the chat service's blocking + streaming use; toolcallback.enabled publishes remote tools as ToolCallback beans. The starter is on the classpath unconditionally but only dials out because a connection is configured here.
nodes.norm_label: chat mcp client config (sync, 30s timeout, toolcallback enabled)

nodes.label: streamable-http connection 'anthropic-courses-tools' -> localhost:8082/mcp
nodes.rationale: URL and endpoint must match mcp-server's own spring.ai.mcp.server config (port 8082, /mcp); keeping this in a profile file means mcp-server being down cannot stop chat from starting.

nodes.label: chat Anthropic API key + model (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, claude-sonnet-4-6)
nodes.norm_label: chat anthropic api key + model (anthropic_api_key, claude-sonnet-4-6)

nodes.label: Prompt-cache strategy (SYSTEM_AND_TOOLS)
nodes.rationale: Enumerated strategies NONE | TOOLS_ONLY | SYSTEM_ONLY | SYSTEM_AND_TOOLS | CONVERSATION_HISTORY; the default caches the stable system prompt and tool definitions, the parts that repeat across requests.

nodes.label: embedding.server.base-url (http://localhost:8081)
nodes.rationale: Single knob used under the rag profile for both retrieval and document upload/list/delete proxying; chunking options deliberately stay on the embedding server side.

nodes.label: chat upload limits (100MB/file, 200MB/request, max-swallow-size -1)
nodes.rationale: max-swallow-size: -1 keeps Tomcat from resetting the connection when rejecting an oversize upload, so the browser receives a clean error instead of a dropped socket.

nodes.label: chat: no autoconfigure excludes needed (VectorStore SPI only)
nodes.norm_label: chat: no autoconfigure excludes needed (vectorstore spi only)

nodes.label: CLAUDE TERMINAL web UI (CRT-styled single-page chat + RAG tabs)
nodes.rationale: Retro-terminal aesthetic (scanline overlay, blinking cursor, monospace, green-on-black) with a two-tab layout; the RAG tab is hidden by default and revealed only when GET /api/ai/documents answers, so one page serves both the rag and non-rag profiles.
nodes.norm_label: claude terminal web ui (crt-styled single-page chat + rag tabs)

nodes.label: Chat form submit flow (params, multipart vs GET, streaming)
nodes.rationale: Attachments force a multipart POST (params travel as form fields) while a plain text message stays a GET with a query string. RAG scoping only sends ragDocumentIds when some documents are unchecked, and an explicitly empty value disables RAG for that request.
nodes.norm_label: chat form submit flow (params, multipart vs get, streaming)

nodes.label: streamInto (SSE reader that appends data: lines)
nodes.norm_label: streaminto (sse reader that appends data: lines)

nodes.label: isAnalysable (client-side guard for code-execution file analysis)
nodes.rationale: Blocks the send locally instead of letting the server reject it, so the typed message is not lost; the checkbox is disabled whenever no loadable file is selected to keep it honest.
nodes.norm_label: isanalysable (client-side guard for code-execution file analysis)

nodes.label: ANALYSIS_EXTENSIONS (mirrors DocumentHelper.ANALYSIS_EXTENSIONS)
nodes.rationale: Duplicated in the browser on purpose so the UI can validate before upload; the comment marks it as a mirror of the server-side Java constant, which is the coupling to keep in sync.

nodes.label: loadDocuments (renders the RAG document table)
nodes.rationale: Each row carries a per-document checkbox whose data-id becomes the ragDocumentIds sent with the next chat request, and HTML is escaped by hand since rows are built by string concatenation.

nodes.label: RAG document delete flow (delegated click, encodeURIComponent id)
nodes.rationale: Event delegation over the table survives re-rendering; the document id is percent-encoded into the path and a 404 is translated to 'already deleted?' rather than a bare HTTP status.
nodes.norm_label: rag document delete flow (delegated click, encodeuricomponent id)

nodes.label: RAG upload flow (multipart files + splitMethod, no page reload)
nodes.rationale: Field name 'files' matches the server @RequestParam; omitting splitMethod lets the server default win. 404 is reported as 'RAG disabled - start the app with the rag profile' and 413 as an upload-limit breach, turning profile/config states into readable UI errors.
nodes.norm_label: rag upload flow (multipart files + splitmethod, no page reload)

nodes.label: conversationId (sessionStorage UUID sent with every request)
nodes.rationale: Conversation memory is keyed client-side: Reset simply mints a new UUID, so clearing the transcript and starting a new server-side conversation are the same action.
nodes.norm_label: conversationid (sessionstorage uuid sent with every request)

nodes.label: THEMES (traffic-light colour switch bound to Tone: KIND/NEUTRAL/RUDE)
nodes.rationale: Colour theme and assistant tone are one control: picking green/orange/red rewrites the CSS custom properties and the hidden tone field together, so the UI's mood always matches the prompt tone sent to the server.
nodes.norm_label: themes (traffic-light colour switch bound to tone: kind/neutral/rude)

nodes.label: Test config: exclude DataSource + PgVectorStore autoconfiguration
nodes.rationale: Without the excludes the pgvector starter's JDBC and vector-store autoconfiguration fails because tests have no datasource.
nodes.norm_label: test config: exclude datasource + pgvectorstore autoconfiguration

nodes.label: Test config: docker compose disabled, embedding model none
nodes.rationale: Tests never start containers and need no embeddings, so Ollama's embedding model is switched off while Claude stays the only ChatModel (Ollama chat autoconfig backs off).
nodes.norm_label: test config: docker compose disabled, embedding model none

nodes.label: compose service: ollama (port 11434, ollama-data volume)
nodes.rationale: Named volume persists the pulled embed model across runs so restarts do not re-download it.

nodes.label: compose service: pgvector/pg17 (ragdb on 5432, pgvector-data volume)
nodes.rationale: Named volume persists ingested document vectors across runs.
nodes.norm_label: compose service: pgvector/pg17 (ragdb on 5432, pgvector-data volume)

nodes.label: Pinned compose project name 'anthropic-courses'
nodes.rationale: Volumes stay named anthropic-courses_* regardless of which directory the compose file lives in, so the pulled embed model and the ingested vectors survive moving the file between modules.

nodes.label: Ollama embedding model nomic-embed-text (pull when_missing)
nodes.rationale: Ollama serves ONLY embeddings here; no chat: none guard is needed because the module declares no chat-model starter at all. The first run pulls the model automatically.

nodes.label: pgvector store config (768 dims, hnsw, cosine_distance, initialize-schema)
nodes.rationale: dimensions: 768 must match nomic-embed-text's output width; initialize-schema uses CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS so it is idempotent and keeps existing rows.
nodes.norm_label: pgvector store config (768 dims, hnsw, cosine_distance, initialize-schema)

nodes.label: rag.splitter default TOKEN (TOKEN | SEMANTIC)
nodes.rationale: TOKEN is the fast default; SEMANTIC is embedding-based and therefore slower, which is also why the HTTP client read-timeout is raised to 5m.

nodes.label: rag.semantic tuning (breakpoint-percentile 95.0, max-chunk-chars 4000)
nodes.rationale: A lower percentile yields more, smaller chunks; the hard character cap keeps every chunk under the embedding model's token limit regardless of where breakpoints fall.

nodes.label: docker.compose.enabled: true + 5m read timeout
nodes.rationale: Boot auto-starts the Ollama + pgvector containers for this module; the long read timeout absorbs semantic chunking's many embedding calls.

nodes.label: MCP server config (anthropic-courses-tools, streamable HTTP at /mcp, port 8082)
nodes.rationale: No autoconfigure excludes and no spring.ai.model.*=none guards: the module's pom declares only the MCP starter, so no datasource, vector store, chat model or embedding model autoconfiguration is on the classpath to begin with.
nodes.norm_label: mcp server config (anthropic-courses-tools, streamable http at /mcp, port 8082)

nodes.label: MCP server instructions (advertise add tool + docs:// resource workflow)
nodes.rationale: Instructions tell the client the two-step read protocol: read docs://mcp-server for the list of document URIs, then read one of them, because templates alone do not enumerate concrete documents.
nodes.norm_label: mcp server instructions (advertise add tool + docs:// resource workflow)

nodes.label: docs folder publication boundary (DocsResources, subfolders included)
nodes.rationale: Everything under mcp-server/src/main/resources/docs is published over MCP and nothing outside it is, giving an explicit, auditable exposure boundary. URIs are relative to that folder, so the docs/ prefix is not part of them.
nodes.norm_label: docs folder publication boundary (docsresources, subfolders included)

nodes.label: Document URI encoding rule (percent-encode slashes in subfolder paths)
nodes.rationale: An MCP URI template variable matches ([^/]+) and stops at a /, so nested paths must arrive percent-encoded (docs://mcp-server/guides%2Furis.md). The listing already emits the encoded form so a client that reads the listing first never applies the rule by hand.
nodes.norm_label: document uri encoding rule (percent-encode slashes in subfolder paths)

nodes.label: El Planeta Tierra (APA 7 formatted Spanish PDF sample)
nodes.rationale: A small, deterministic, generated letter-size PDF with APA margins, a title, two body paragraphs, a references section and a formatting note - shaped as a realistic RAG/document-upload fixture rather than as real scholarship.
nodes.norm_label: el planeta tierra (apa 7 formatted spanish pdf sample)

nodes.label: Earth (third planet from the Sun, densest, fifth largest)
nodes.rationale: Claimed as the largest of the four terrestrial/rocky planets, interacting closely with the Sun and with the Moon, its only natural satellite.
nodes.norm_label: earth (third planet from the sun, densest, fifth largest)

nodes.label: Citation: Tierra. (2026, 18 de julio). En Wikipedia
nodes.norm_label: citation: tierra. (2026, 18 de julio). en wikipedia

nodes.label: APA 7 note on citing Wikipedia (title in the author slot)
nodes.rationale: The article title takes the author position because a wiki article is collectively authored; the exact revision date and, where possible, a link to the archived history version are included so the reader reaches exactly the same text. Hanging indent is mandatory in APA references.
nodes.norm_label: apa 7 note on citing wikipedia (title in the author slot)
